ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the schematic diagram of the distribution of partial solar altitude on latitude lines L1 and L2. <image1> If L1 and L2 are both located in the Northern Hemisphere, and H=80°, then what is the latitude range of latitude line L1?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled “solar altitude”, the bottom horizontal axis indicates the direction along the latitude line, and the right side is labeled “east”. In the figure there are two solar altitude variation curves, L1 and L2; both reach the same highest solar altitude H at the middle M; the L2 curve approaches or drops to 0° at the left and right ends, while the L1 curve is still higher than 0° at the same left and right positions, so it can be read that the day length of the latitude line where L1 is located is longer than that of L2. Then reason: It is known that H=80°, and the noon solar altitude formula is H=90°-|φ-δ|, so |φ-δ|=10°. L1 and L2 are both in the Northern Hemisphere and have the same noon solar altitude, indicating that the two latitude lines are located on the north and south sides of the direct-sun latitude δ, that is, the latitudes are respectively δ-10° and δ+10°. From the figure, L1 has a longer day length; when the direct sun is in the Northern Hemisphere, in the Northern Hemisphere the higher the latitude, the longer the day length, so L1 should be the higher latitude line, namely φ1=δ+10°. Also, L2 is located in the Northern Hemisphere, so δ-10°≥0°, that is, δ≥10°; the northernmost direct-sun point does not exceed 23.5°N, that is, δ≤23.5°. Therefore, the range of φ1=δ+10° is from 20°N to 33.5°N.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the schematic diagram of the distribution of partial solar altitude on latitude lines L1 and L2.

<image1>

If L1 and L2 are both located in the Northern Hemisphere, and H=80°, then what is the latitude range of latitude line L1?

method.method_draft: 先读图：纵轴为太阳高度，横轴表示沿纬线由西向东的方向；L1、L2两条纬线上的太阳高度曲线在M处达到同一个最大值H；L2曲线在左右两侧降到0°，而L1在相同位置仍高于0°，说明L1昼长比L2长。再读题：L1、L2都在北半球，且H=80°。用正午太阳高度公式H=90°-|φ-δ|，得|φ-δ|=10°。两条北半球纬线正午高度相同，故它们分别在太阳直射纬度δ的南北两侧：φ=δ-10°与φ=δ+10°。由图中L1昼长更长，且北半球昼长随纬度升高而增大时对应太阳直射北半球，所以L1为较高纬，即φ1=δ+10°。又L2仍在北半球，δ-10°≥0°，并且太阳直射点最北不超过23.5°N，即δ≤23.5°。所以φ1=δ+10°的范围为20°N~33.5°N。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Read the schematic diagram of the distribution of partial solar altitude on latitude lines L1 and L2.

<image1>

If L1 and L2 are both located in the Northern Hemisphere, and H=80°, then what is the latitude range of latitude line L1?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the schematic diagram of the distribution of partial solar altitude on latitude lines L1 and L2. <image1> If L1 and L2 are both located in the Northern Hemisphere, and H=80°, then what is the latitude range of latitude line L1?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled “solar altitude”, the bottom horizontal axis indicates the direction along the latitude line, and the right side is labeled “east”. In the figure there are two solar altitude variation curves, L1 and L2; both reach the same highest solar altitude H at the middle M; the L2 curve approaches or drops to 0° at the left and right ends, while the L1 curve is still higher than 0° at the same left and right positions, so it can be read that the day length of the latitude line where L1 is located is longer than that of L2.
Then reason: It is known that H=80°, and the noon solar altitude formula is H=90°-|φ-δ|, so |φ-δ|=10°. L1 and L2 are both in the Northern Hemisphere and have the same noon solar altitude, indicating that the two latitude lines are located on the north and south sides of the direct-sun latitude δ, that is, the latitudes are respectively δ-10° and δ+10°. From the figure, L1 has a longer day length; when the direct sun is in the Northern Hemisphere, in the Northern Hemisphere the higher the latitude, the longer the day length, so L1 should be the higher latitude line, namely φ1=δ+10°. Also, L2 is located in the Northern Hemisphere, so δ-10°≥0°, that is, δ≥10°; the northernmost direct-sun point does not exceed 23.5°N, that is, δ≤23.5°. Therefore, the range of φ1=δ+10° is from 20°N to 33.5°N.
